input_signals.name: ProfitPerAccrualBloat
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Cumulative past accruals are embodied in the stock of net operating assets, so gross profit measured per dollar of accrual-accumulated operating capital separates firms that earn profits on a lean balance sheet from firms whose reported profits rest on a bloated receivable/inventory/net-operating-asset base that must eventually be written down.
input_signals.reasoning: Unlike a small additive perturbation of total assets, the deflator here is materially different — it strips cash and nets out operating liabilities — so the accrual channel drives large cross-sectional variation rather than acting cosmetically. It converts the accrual theme from a flow to a stock concept (balance-sheet bloat) and asks how much true trading profit that accrual stock supports, which is a distinct mechanism from period accruals.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), sub( sub( at, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: ProfitVsAccrualBloatTrend
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), SIGN(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Multi-year accumulation of net operating assets, not the single-year accrual flow, reveals whether a profitable firm is steadily capitalizing costs and stretching working capital; sustained profitability with a shrinking operating-asset base is genuinely cash-generative, while the same profitability with a rising base is accounting-driven and reverses.
input_signals.reasoning: Replacing the one-year accrual with a three-year trend in the accrual stock tests a slow-moving accounting-aggressiveness state that annual accrual flows measure noisily, while smoothing profitability with MA(·,3) matches the horizon of the credibility question. The sign-conditioning again concentrates the long and short legs among persistently profitable firms, so the spread is an accrual-quality bet, not a profitability bet.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ) ), sign( neg( trend( ratio( sub( sub( at, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: AccrualGradedProfitability
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Accrual intensity does not merely add to profitability information, it scales it: the higher a firm's profitability, the more its future returns depend on whether those profits were accompanied by large or small balance-sheet accruals, so the accrual measure should enter as a graded multiplier on the profitability signal.
input_signals.reasoning: The non-negative profitability rank multiplied by a mean-zero, industry-standardized accrual-quality score produces a pure interaction: unprofitable firms are compressed toward zero regardless of accruals, while the long and short tails are both highly profitable firms separated by accrual magnitude — so a positive result cannot be explained by either main effect alone. It also isolates one specific design choice against the accepted sign-conditioned signal: whether graded accrual intensity carries information beyond the mere sign of working-capital accruals.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), neg( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ), dp ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CashAdjProfitPerAccrualBloat
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1))), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Durable profitability is cash operating profit — reported operating income minus the working-capital accrual that inflated it — measured per dollar of the accrual-accumulated operating capital that had to be tied up to earn it; both the flow and the stock of accruals must be charged against profits.
input_signals.reasoning: This keeps the deflator that produced the archive's best portfolio alpha but replaces the raw profit numerator with a materially cash-adjusted one (the accrual subtraction is comparable in size to the profit itself, unlike gen-0's trivial denominator perturbation), so the accrual channel now enters twice and in the same economic direction. It tests whether the GP/NOA result strengthens when the numerator is also purged of accrual content, which distinguishes the "accrual bloat" story from a plain profitability-per-capital story.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( sub( oibdp, sub( delta( sub( act, che ), 1 ), delta( sub( lct, dlc ), 1 ) ) ), sub( sub( at, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: UnexpectedAccrualGradedProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), MA(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 5)), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Only the *unexpected* part of accruals signals earnings that will reverse: a growing firm normally accrues working capital every year, so what discredits reported profits is an accrual this year far above the firm's own established accrual norm, which is the symptom of discretionary revenue pulling-forward rather than of business expansion.
input_signals.reasoning: Rather than rank-wrapping the archived signal, this changes the accrual construct itself from a cross-sectional level to a firm-specific abnormal-accrual deviation from a five-year norm, which is the standard discretionary-accrual identification idea and is economically distinct from Sloan-level accruals. The multiplier remains a signed industry z-score so the conditional sign-flip mechanism is preserved, and because abnormal accruals are far less persistent than accrual levels, the resulting portfolio should reshuffle on genuine accounting-quality news rather than on slow-moving firm characteristics — the plausible reason the level-graded version had a strong slope but a muted FF5 alpha.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), neg( ind_zscore( winsor( sub( ratio( sub( delta( sub( act, che ), 1 ), delta( sub( lct, dlc ), 1 ) ), at ), ma( ratio( sub( delta( sub( act, che ), 1 ), delta( sub( lct, dlc ), 1 ) ), at ), 5 ) ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CollectionBackedProfitMargin
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(recch, invch), sale), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Under the Compustat decrease-positive convention, positive RECCH+INVCH means receivables and inventory released cash, so profitable firms whose working capital is being collected and sold down have genuinely converted profits into cash, while equally profitable firms whose receivables and inventory absorb cash relative to sales are recognizing revenue ahead of collection and will reverse.
input_signals.reasoning: The direction is now set by the documented sign convention rather than by back-fitting to the earlier inverted t-stat, and if the archive's inversion was real it will show up here as a clean, interpretable rejection of the convention rather than as a hidden fudge. Deflating the receivable/inventory flow by sales rather than assets matches the channel-stuffing mechanism (working capital absorbed per dollar of revenue booked) and makes the conditioner comparable across capital intensities.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( add( recch, invch ), sale ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: DepreciationBackedProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dpc, at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that still earn strong profits *after* absorbing heavy non-cash depreciation charges are conservatively stated: their accrual accounting subtracts more from reported income than cash economics require, so their earnings are understated and more persistent than those of equally profitable firms carrying negligible non-cash charges.
input_signals.reasoning: Switching the profitability leg to post-depreciation operating income (oiadp) removes the internal inconsistency: the interaction now identifies firms whose profitability survives the conservative charge, not firms whose EBITDA is flattered by it. Industry standardization of dpc/at absorbs the bulk of the capital-intensity variation in D&A, leaving within-industry differences in depreciation aggressiveness as the conditioning variable, which is precisely the accrual-conservatism concept being tested.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( dpc, at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: ProfitVsExcessWCGrowth
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(GROWTH(SUB(act, che), 1), GROWTH(sale, 1)), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The right benchmark for accrual growth is sales growth: a profitable firm whose receivables and inventory grow faster than revenue is granting looser credit or accumulating unsold goods, so its profits are accrual-inflated, while a profitable firm whose working capital grows slower than sales is scaling on real demand.
input_signals.reasoning: All prior accrual conditioners were deflated by assets, which conflates efficient growth with accrual manipulation; benchmarking working-capital growth against sales growth removes the growth component and leaves the abnormal-accrual component, a normalization never tested in the archive. Because the conditioner is a growth differential rather than a level, it should also carry fresher information than the slow-moving bloat state while remaining economically the same credibility test.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), neg( ind_zscore( winsor( sub( growth( sub( act, che ), 1 ), growth( sale, 1 ) ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: ShortCycleProfitability
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Profits earned with a short (or negative) cash conversion cycle are the most credible: when customers pay before suppliers must be paid, reported profit converts into cash almost immediately and cannot have been manufactured by extending customer credit or stockpiling inventory, whereas the same profit earned with many days of working capital outstanding is accrual-dependent and reverts.
input_signals.reasoning: The conditioner is net operating working capital expressed in days of sales — a cash-conversion-cycle concept — rather than the one-year accrual flow whose sign the archive has already tested in both directions, so nothing about its outcome is implied by existing results. Deflating by sales instead of assets is also the economically right normalization for an operating-cycle length and separates the idea from the net-operating-asset/asset-growth family the critic flagged.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), neg( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), sale ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: PeakProfitAccrualRegime
input_signals.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), NEG(ZSCORE(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Profitability at a multi-year high is trustworthy only when the firm's working-capital intensity is simultaneously at a multi-year low; peak profits accompanied by historically elevated receivables and inventory are the classic signature of pulled-forward revenue and revert, while peak profits on a historically lean operating cycle reflect a genuine improvement in earning power.
input_signals.reasoning: Both legs are measured as positions in the firm's own five-year history, which is a regime concept absent from the archive (all prior signals used cross-sectional levels, one-year flows, or growth differentials) and which directly targets the reversal question the task poses. The profitability leg is a non-negative own-history percentile and the accrual leg a mean-zero cross-sectional standardization of an own-history percentile, so the extremes are firms at profitability peaks separated by whether their accrual intensity is also peaking — a true interaction with no single-ratio delta and no small-denominator differencing.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ts_rank( ratio( oibdp, at ), 5 ), neg( zscore( ts_rank( ratio( sub( act, che ), sale ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CumulativeAccrualGradedProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(TS_SUM(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 5), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: What discredits a profitable firm is not the size of its operating asset base per se but how much of that base was built by accruals: five years of accumulated working-capital accruals measures the portion of the balance sheet created by accounting recognition rather than by capital investment, and profits resting on that accumulation are the ones that reverse.
input_signals.reasoning: This directly addresses the critic's concern that NOA-based conditioners reproduce the published net-operating-asset anomaly: cumulating the accrual flow isolates the accounting-created portion of operating capital while excluding the legitimate installed capital and initial endowment embedded in the NOA level. It also converts the flow family (strong slopes, weak alpha) into a slow-moving state without borrowing the NOA level itself, giving a clean test of which stock definition drives the alpha.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ) ), neg( ind_zscore( winsor( ts_sum( ratio( sub( delta( sub( act, che ), 1 ), delta( sub( lct, dlc ), 1 ) ), at ), 5 ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: ChronicAccrualGradedProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 3), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Chronic accrual reliance, not a single year's accrual, is what marks profits as unsustainable: a firm that has expanded working capital faster than it collected cash for three consecutive years is systematically recognizing revenue ahead of cash, and its profitability should command no premium.
input_signals.reasoning: This repairs the archive's most consistent failure mode — flow-graded interactions with strong slopes (fmb 4.7) but negligible alpha (1.5%) — by converting the transient one-year accrual into a persistent three-year accounting-policy state that can sustain a stable long-short portfolio. If the alpha rises while the slope holds, we learn the flow family failed on portfolio persistence rather than on economics, which would redirect the remaining generations toward smoothed flow conditioners.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), neg( ind_zscore( winsor( ma( ratio( sub( delta( sub( act, che ), 1 ), delta( sub( lct, dlc ), 1 ) ), at ), 3 ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: AbnormalWCDaysProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), MA(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), 5)), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Every firm has a structural working-capital cycle determined by its industry and business model; what discredits reported profits is a stretch in receivable and inventory days *relative to the firm's own established cycle*, because that deviation cannot be explained by the operating model and must reflect looser credit terms or unsold output.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a new conditioning construct rather than a blend: it measures the accrual state as a stock in days of sales (the family that has produced the archive's tradable alphas) but benchmarks it against the firm's own five-year norm (the normalization that has produced the archive's strongest Fama-MacBeth slopes), which is precisely the combination the evidence says is missing. Because the deviation is firm-centered, it also avoids the cross-sectional industry tilt that makes level-based bloat conditioners resemble the published net-operating-asset anomaly.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), neg( ind_zscore( winsor( sub( ratio( sub( act, che ), sale ), ma( ratio( sub( act, che ), sale ), 5 ) ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: WeakestLinkQualityProfit
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Earnings credibility is conjunctive, not additive: a firm qualifies as durably profitable only if it clears both hurdles — high profit per dollar of accrual-accumulated capital *and* no current-year accrual inflation — and failing either one is sufficient to make its profits suspect, regardless of how strong the other looks.
input_signals.reasoning: A minimum of two industry ranks is a weakest-link aggregation that no archive signal uses and that behaves nothing like an ensemble: averaging lets a strong accrual score rescue weak bloat-adjusted profitability, whereas MIN does not, so the long leg contains only firms credible on both dimensions and the result identifies whether the market prices joint credibility rather than either component. Both inputs are bounded industry percentiles, which should keep the Fama-MacBeth slope and the decile spread reading the same ordering — the divergence that has plagued the unbounded product designs.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), sub( sub( at, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ) ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( neg( winsor( ratio( sub( delta( sub( act, che ), 1 ), delta( sub( lct, dlc ), 1 ) ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: TripleHurdleQualityProfit
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)), MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at), 3), 1))), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, act), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Durable profitability requires clearing three independent credibility hurdles — high profit per dollar of accrual-accumulated capital, no chronic multi-year accrual reliance, and current assets actually realized into cash — and firms failing any one of them hold earnings that will reverse.
input_signals.reasoning: Each added hurdle is drawn from an independently validated channel (bloat ratio alpha 4.1%, chronic accrual state alpha 3.4% with Sharpe 0.40, cash realization alpha 5.4%), and because MIN is conjunctive rather than averaging, the third screen removes firms that pass on two dimensions rather than diluting them, which is not achievable by blending. The risk is that a triple minimum concentrates the long leg too narrowly, so the diagnostic value lies in comparing its Sharpe and alpha t-stat against the two-hurdle version.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), sub( sub( at, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ) ), 1 ) ), min( ind_rank( neg( winsor( ma( ratio( sub( delta( sub( act, che ), 1 ), delta( sub( lct, dlc ), 1 ) ), at ), 3 ), 1 ) ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( che, act ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.hypothesis: The two strongest forms of accrual validation are structural (profit earned per dollar of accrual-bloated capital) and realizational (current assets converted into cash); a firm must satisfy both, because capital-efficient profits held entirely in receivables are as suspect as cash-rich firms with no earning power.
input_signals.reasoning: This substitutes the accrual *stock realization* channel for the accrual *flow* channel inside the winning conjunctive structure, testing whether the weakest-link result depends on the specific flow measure or generalizes across accrual concepts. Because the cash-realization channel previously delivered a 5.4% alpha with a wrong-signed slope, embedding it in bounded ranks also tests whether conjunctive rank construction repairs that divergence.

input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), sub( sub( at, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ) ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( che, act ), 1 ) ) )

The comparison is essential for interpretation: if performance is preserved, the mechanism is joint credibility screening; if it collapses, the accrual-stock deflator is doing the work and later refinements should target the deflator.

input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_ZSCORE(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1)), at)), 0), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Consistency of cash backing, not its average magnitude, certifies profits: a firm that has released rather than absorbed working capital in most of the last five years has demonstrated a repeatable cash-generative operating model, whereas the same average accrual achieved through one large swing reveals nothing about durability.

input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(sale, SUB(act, che)), 1)))

input_signals.reasoning: This is a new economic decomposition rather than an aggregation swap — it splits profitability into the margin dimension and makes the accrual dimension the *turnover velocity of accrual assets*, a quantity no archive signal has used, so neither leg is one of the published anomalies the critic identified. Both legs are bounded industry percentiles and jointly required, the structure that just produced the archive's only signal strong on the cross-sectional slope, the FF5 alpha, and the Sharpe simultaneously.
